newsitem.title: USA: Marion Capital raises div, OK's buyback.
newsitem.headline: Marion Capital raises div, OK's buyback.

text.p: Marion Capital Holdings Inc said Tuesday it raised its quarterly cash dividend by 10 percent, to $0.22 a share from $0.20.

The company also said its board of directors approved the repurchase of up to 87,905 shares, or five percent, of the company's outstanding stock. The board authorized spending up to $2 million on the buyback program.
The dividend is payable on June 13 to shareholders of record on May 30, the company said.
Marion said the share repurchases will be made subject to market conditions in the open market or in block transations. Repurchases may begin immediately, the company said.

The board "believes that the corporation's shares are from time to time undervalued by the market and that open market purchases will have the effect of enhancing the book value per share and the potential for growth in earnings per share of the corporation's remaining outstanding shares," the company said in a statement.
Marion has completed seven other stock buyback programs including one completed this month which reduced the number of outstanding shares to 1,758,096.
Marion is the holding company for First Federal Savings Bank of Marion.
